newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BONNITA SHARES SOUR ON LOWER YR EARNINGS.
newsitem.headline: BONNITA SHARES SOUR ON LOWER YR EARNINGS.

text.p: Shares in South African dairy firm Bonnita Ltd fell at the start of trading on Monday after the firm announced a dip in year earnings on Friday following a milk shortage.
By 0945 GMT shares were down nine percent or 27 cents to 273 cents, making it the biggest percentage loser on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in early dealings.
"Bonnita's obviously down on the results," one dealer said.
The Western Cape-based company on Friday reported year share earnings at 27.2 cents, down from 30.1 cents a year ago. The dividend was held at 9.5 cents.

The group, however, spoke of growth prospects in the new financial year. It said that a new factory would be established in Gauteng, giving the group access to another 40 percent of the country's raw milk.
Although expected high milk prices would continue affecting profit margins, Bonnita said it was confident that market forces would prevail.
"The (share) price should get back onto track as the group is likely to resume normal good earnings again," a trader said.
